London said her recent visit to Nigeria was strictly for a documentary project and to experience the country firsthand, insisting that neither the Federal Government nor any individual in Nigeria paid her the alleged amount.
She stated this in a post on her X account on Wednesday, following public discussions surrounding her recent engagement with President Bola Tinubu and allegations about her involvement in Nigeria’s lobbying arrangement in the United States.
Dismissing the claims, London said attempts to link her to the reported payment would not change the circumstances of her visit or prevent her from speaking out.
“I unequivocally deny the claim that Nigeria’s government nor anyone else in Nigeria paid me $4.5 million.
“I went to Nigeria to interview President Tinubu @officialABAT for parts of a documentary and see Nigeria for myself.
“This SMEAR CAMPAIGN can make noise, but can’t change the facts or stop me from speaking the truth,” she stated.
The controversy followed reports linking London to an alleged $4.5 million payment under a lobbying arrangement involving the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu.
However, the allegation has also drawn attention to the distinction between payments reportedly made to her company and a separate $4.5 million advance payment Nigeria allegedly made to DCI Group, an American lobbying firm engaged by the Federal Government.
London is the Chief Executive Officer of London Global Strategies, a government affairs and crisis communications firm.
Despite the controversy, she has maintained that her visit to Nigeria was to interview Tinubu for a documentary and gain firsthand knowledge of the country.
She also insisted that the allegations would not deter her from expressing her views or continuing her work.
